summary: Inline round-3 review: all four prior blockers are partially addressed, but credential isolation, pending-state integrity, mutation retries and account-stop handling still have concrete safety gaps. Type-checking passed and targeted offline reproductions confirmed several failures. No live Instagram calls were made; the full Bun suite was not run because its fixtures require filesystem writes.

prior_blockers.title: Credential isolation still fails open
prior_blockers.evidence: Directories are now protected before cookie storage or Chrome launch (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/cookie-store.ts:120; auth.ts:238). However, secure.ts:48 treats any DOMAIN\<same username> as the current principal. A mocked ACL containing a different domain account with that username returned ok:true without removing its grant.

prior_blockers.title: GraphQL discovery does not establish usable read contracts
prior_blockers.evidence: Variables, adapters and cursor pagination now exist (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/graphql.ts:160; read.ts:117), and embedded results identify their limited sample. Response-root selection remains heuristic (graphql.ts:178), without representative operation/pagination fixtures. The live read test accepts an empty array and does not exercise pagination (test/live.test.ts:36). Actual Instagram compatibility remains unverified.

prior_blockers.title: Mutation schemas and verification gates remain incomplete
prior_blockers.evidence: Payload construction is substantially more explicit, including ordered children and story upload_id (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/publish.ts:225,291). Story/delete/comment/reply receive an experimental gate, but photo/carousel/reel/edit bypass it solely through observed-in-bundle labels (publish.ts:20; main.ts:123). No successful live mutation evidence is supplied, and test/live.test.ts:45 covers only photo/delete.

prior_blockers.title: Caption-based recovery cannot safely reconcile ambiguous writes
prior_blockers.evidence: Recovery now correctly lists candidates without auto-resolving, handles stories manually, and requires explicit resolution (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/publish.ts:404; main.ts:368). Ordinary ambiguous configure failures retain a pending record (publish.ts:441). However, pending.ts:55,63 silently ignores unreadable or corrupt ledger state, and configure can still replay an ambiguous accepted response.

strengths: Authenticated requests enforce HTTPS and an Instagram hostname allowlist, with redirects disabled; no session-bearing path to a non-Instagram host was found (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/client.ts:199; constants.ts:22). GraphQL bundle fetches omit cookies (graphql.ts:85).

Valid and invalid photo dry runs, delete/reply previews, and the delete experimental gate passed targeted subprocess fetch-trap checks. Normal previews contain no session cookies or GraphQL tokens (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/main.ts:131,348; publish.ts:297).

Ordinary network/5xx/HTML publish failures are not automatically retried and preserve recovery state; caption matches never resolve it automatically (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/publish.ts:434,404).

Direct REST account signals stop fallback chains. Research enforces 12 accounts and 50 posts per account; authenticated requests default to 1.5-second pacing (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/client.ts:98,284; main.ts:301,307).
No like, follow or DM commands were found. TypeScript noEmit validation passed.

blocking_findings.title: Windows isolation accepts a different account with the same username
blocking_findings.why: A distinct local/domain account can retain an explicit credential-directory grant while storage protection reports success. This violates the current-user-only boundary before cookies or browser credentials are stored.
blocking_findings.evidence: isSelf accepts every principal ending in the current username, regardless of domain. Both grant removal and final verification use that predicate. A mocked ACL containing CURRENTDOMAIN\user and OTHERDOMAIN\user returned ok:true with zero removal calls. Identity must be compared using the actual principal/SID.

blocking_findings.title: Corrupt or unreadable pending state silently permits another publish
blocking_findings.why: A failed or interrupted ledger update can erase the only protection against repeating an already committed publish. Unknown recovery state must block publishing rather than appear empty.
blocking_findings.evidence: listPending returns [] on every readdir error and ignores every unreadable or invalid JSON record. markUnresolved overwrites the existing record directly, so interruption after truncation can create exactly this condition. An in-memory reproduction with a truncated pending JSON record returned []. executePlan relies on that list to decide whether publishing is safe.

blocking_findings.title: Ambiguous mutation responses can trigger a second write automatically
blocking_findings.why: A response that does not establish failure can follow a committed mutation. Replaying it without verified idempotency risks duplicate posts or comments and exceeds approval for one comment.
blocking_findings.evidence: classifyBody treats every HTTP 202 as transcode_pending, even an otherwise successful response containing a media ID; configure then repeats the POST. A mocked 202 with media.pk produced two configure POSTs. Separately, addComment uses tryEach: a successful response missing the expected comment ID becomes unexpected_response and triggers the alternate creation endpoint. A mocked status:ok response without an ID produced two comment POSTs. The bounded transcode loop also makes up to 11 configure attempts, rather than the plan's stated 10.

blocking_findings.title: Unproven mutations remain outside the experimental gate
blocking_findings.why: Observing endpoint and field names does not validate payload encoding or resulting behavior. The prior requirement to keep each unproven mutation behind an explicit experimental opt-in remains unmet.
blocking_findings.evidence: Photo, carousel, reel and editCaption are labelled observed-in-bundle, and requireGate rejects only unverified. Those operations therefore execute with --confirm alone despite the plan acknowledging that no write has been verified live. Current tests assert the chosen labels and generated bodies rather than establish their Instagram contracts.

blocking_findings.title: Some checkpoint responses do not stop subsequent account requests
blocking_findings.why: A checkpoint or authentication restriction can be treated as an ordinary endpoint failure, causing further requests against an account that should have stopped.
blocking_findings.evidence: GraphQL errors are examined only when data is absent, and their messages distinguish only rate/limit from bad_request. A mocked challenge_required error became bad_request; getPosts explicitly catches that kind and requests the embedded-profile fallback. HTML checkpoint pages similarly become unexpected_response, which tryEach permits to fall through. Partial GraphQL data suppresses error handling altogether.

non_blocking_findings.title: The live-test preload discards the session required by the documented test command
non_blocking_findings.why: The supplied acceptance harness cannot validate the real session as documented, weakening the evidence needed to promote contracts.
non_blocking_findings.evidence: test/bunfig.toml preloads unit/setup.ts for live tests too. That setup always replaces INSTAGRAM_DATA_DIR with an empty temporary directory and deletes INSTAGRAM_COOKIES. Consequently, the documented live command loses both supported session sources before IgClient.create. This conclusion is source-derived; no live test was executed.

open_questions: No live Instagram calls were made. Do sanitized successful requests and responses establish each configure payload, encoding, response shape and pagination contract?
What verified server behavior establishes that each retryable configure response means no publication has committed, or that replaying the same upload_id is idempotent?
After correcting the live harness, which operations will pass their own approved acceptance tests before being promoted beyond experimental?
